name: Nextify.ai
summary: AI ad-video generator for advertisers and e-commerce sellers: turn a product image, a script or a brief into a vertical or landscape video ad, with avatar presenters, lip-sync, product image sets and image cloning in the same workspace. Eight tools in one credit pool — Create Video Ad, Viral Video, Video Cloning, UGC Product Video, Lip-sync, Image Generator, Listing Images and Image Cloning — running on Seedance, Kling, MiniMax, HeyGen, GPT Image and Nano Banana models you pick per generation. Metered in credits per second of output rather than per finished video, with the cost shown on the generate button before you commit.
best_for: advertisers who need a steady stream of short product clips and will deliberately choose the cheap model for drafts, and teams who would rather have video, avatars, lip-sync and product imagery drawing on one credit pool than pay for four separate subscriptions
skip_if: you are budgeting from the “up to N videos” figures on the pricing page, you need talking-head or avatar video at any volume — that route is 6.7 credits a second, so Pro buys seven sixty-second ads a month — or you expected the free tier to work as a trial: it is 50 watermarked credits and it cannot reach the Seedance models at all
honest_knock: The plans are sold in videos and images; the meter runs in credits per second, and the two do not reconcile. Every tier's headline count works out at 20 credits a video and 2 credits an image — 1,000 credits become “up to 50 videos” and “up to 500 images”, 3,000 become 150 and 1,500, 8,000 become 400 and 4,000. The app's own credit table prices video per second of output: Seedance 2.0, the model the editor pre-selects, is 12 credits a second at 720p, so the default four-second clip costs 48. We generated one and watched the balance fall from 3,000 to 2,952. That makes Pro 62 clips a month rather than 150, and 16 if you use the 15-second maximum. The 20-credit figure is reachable, but only on the 5-credit-a-second model at four seconds. The image claim has no such escape hatch: the cheapest image model in the table is 7 credits and the pre-selected one is 10, so nothing in the product costs the 2 credits those counts assume, and Starter's 500 images is nearer 100.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 7 September 2026 on nextify.ai/pricing, signed in and signed out, in both billing modes) Five ways to pay, and the free plan is only visible when you are logged out — the signed-in pricing page starts at Starter. Free is $0 for 50 credits a month, watermarked, on the basic models only, and the page sells that as up to 2 videos and 25 images. Billed monthly the paid tiers are Starter $29, Pro $79 and Business $189. Billed annually the same tiers are $21, $52 and $114 a month, charged $244, $617 and $1,361 a year — the 30%, 35% and 40% badges check out at 28%, 34% and 40% against the monthly rate. Credit allowances are 1,000, 3,000 and 8,000 a month; Business is the only tier with a second seat. A one-off pack of 1,250 credits is $50, never expires and does not auto-renew, which works out at $0.04 a credit against $0.017 on annual Pro — so topping up costs more than twice what the subscription does. Subscription credits do not roll over between cycles. Refunds are limited to three days from a first subscription, and add-on packs are non-refundable.

compare_with.name: Pippit
compare_with.why: the alternative people weigh this against — Pippit is CapCut's credit-metered AI ad maker, and the split is what the meter punishes. Pippit's buyers report credits consumed by generations that failed; Nextify charges predictably per second and shows the cost on the button before you commit, but prices that second well above what its own plan counts imply
